# PM-089: which of PM-088's implementable functions other contributors' open PRs already cover
from: AnyPS5 Project Manager
for: any
priority: normal

## Why
PM-088 (cloud-3, `results/cloud-3/PM-088.md` and `results/cloud-3/PM-088/*.tsv` on `cloud-results`) classified the 4,172 todo functions of the 25 largest libraries on upstream main a6dcea927. A + B-S alone would take the System libraries badge from 42.33% to ~48.6%.

But many other contributors already have open upstream PRs on exactly these libraries. A title search on 2026-10-21 17:55 PT found open PRs on libkernel_sys (33), libSceNet (20), libSceCesCs (10), libSceLibreSsl (9), libSceNpManager (5), libScePad (5), libSceFont (5), libSceNpCppWebApi (4), libSceSystemService (4), libSceNpTus (3) and libSceSaveData (2). Several match PM-088's proposed batches one for one, for example #8923 (27 single-byte code page profiles), #9025 (MD4/MD5/SHA digests), #9448 (EVP digest + HMAC), #8264 (InGameCatalog/TitleCloudStorage IntrusivePtr), #8354 (the running title's app id), #9200 (lchmod), #9008 (fstat).

We don't open competing PRs. So before any batch is chosen we need the unclaimed set: PM-088's implementable rows that no open PR already changes.

Read-only analysis. No build is needed. Reading other contributors' PR heads with git is fine; don't build or run their code.

## Steps
1. Fetch upstream main and the heads of the open PRs listed at the end (1,136 PRs open at 2026-10-22 00:55 UTC): `git fetch upstream main` and `git fetch upstream refs/pull/<N>/head:refs/remotes/upstream-pr/<N>` for each, in batches. Use `upstream`, never `origin`. A PR whose head no longer fetches is skipped and listed.
2. For each PR, `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base upstream/main upstream-pr/<N>) upstream-pr/<N>` and keep the PRs that touch any of the 25 libraries' directories under `core/libs/prx/` (including `.native` and module variants).
3. For each kept PR, find which of that library's PM-088 todo functions it changes: a function whose body in the PR head no longer calls `NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`, or whose body the PR changes. `tools/progress.py`'s parser on the PR head, compared with main's, is the most reliable way. Also note any PR that adds new declared exports (for example #9504 "declare 150 PS5 pending exports"), since declarations lower the badge.
4. Mark every PM-088 row of class A, B-S, B-M and C (real behaviour) as `claimed by #N (author)` or `unclaimed`. A function claimed by more than one PR lists all of them.
5. Re-batch the **unclaimed** rows only: PR-sized batches of 10-40 functions on one topic, with the tests each would carry (reuse PM-088's test plans). Drop any batch that would edit the same function body as an open PR, and say so.
6. Badge estimates with `progress.py`'s formula: (a) if every open PR in step 2 merged as it stands, (b) then also our unclaimed A + B-S batches, (c) then also unclaimed B-M and C-real.

## Result
`results/cloud-<n>/PM-089.md` on `cloud-results`, text only:
- a per-library table: PM-088's A/B-S/B-M/C-real counts, how many are claimed, how many unclaimed;
- the list of open PRs found in step 2 with the functions each claims;
- the unclaimed batch proposals with tests;
- the badge estimates (a)-(c).
Per-function TSVs (`function, class, claimed_by`) go in `results/cloud-<n>/PM-089/`.
